description:
FILED s470bp (Opus, 2026-09-05) while #1188 made the MODULE cache store fasls.
NOT TAKEN in that session because the USER has PARKED the extension load with
pack/unpack (plan-speed-and-ir-s470 §A.0: "the transpiled oracle and its 3 s
extension load are not touched until the XS question is answered").  This task
records the measurement and the (small) design so the answer is one commit
away if the park lifts — or so it can be closed if pclxs carries pack.

THE MEASUREMENT (this box, module fasl cache ON, everything else warm):

    pcl -E 'print pack("N",1) eq "\0\0\0\1" ? 1 : 0'    8.3 s
    pcl -E 'print scalar(@{mro::get_linear_isa("main")})'  0.63 s
    pcl -E 'print 1'                                    0.164 s   (control)

`p-load-extension` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) does a plain `(load file)` of a
CHECKED-IN TRANSPILED .lisp from the tree — cl/pcl-pack.lisp (the biggest of
the three artifacts), cl/pcl-mro.lisp, cl/pcl-warnings.lisp, cl/pcl-xs.lisp —
so SBCL recompiles the whole artifact on EVERY first pack/mro/warnings call,
which is precisely the cost #1188 removed for modules.

THE DESIGN is the #1188 machinery with a different key.  An extension is not a
transpiled MODULE keyed by a perl source's mtime; it is a .lisp file in the
tree, so its cache key is its OWN content (or path+mtime+size) plus
*pcl-runtime-identity* — the generation string does not apply (the artifact is
checked in, and Pl/t/artifact-staleness-01.t already gates its `gen=` stamp
against the generation).  Reuse %p-build-module-fasl / %p-load-module-fasl
verbatim; bind *PCL-FASL-BUILD* the same way (an artifact contains p-sub and
p-BEGIN forms exactly as a module does).

WHAT MUST STILL HOLD: %pcl-check-extension-clean — an extension may install
DEFINITIONS and nothing else, and a fasl must not smuggle a program preamble
past that check (task #349/#217).  The check reads @INC / *pcl-pl2cl-path* /
*p-core-inc-dirs* AFTER the load, so it works unchanged on a fasl load; the
row to add is that a fasl built from an artifact WITHOUT `pl2cl --extension`
still dies there.

EXPECTED PRIZE: pack's 8.3 s to roughly startup + the artifact's load-time
work.  That is the single largest absolute number this session measured, which
is why it is written down even though it is parked.

================================================================
=== THE PARK'S PREMISE HAS MOVED (s473x, 2026-09-19, Opus) â THIS COST IS
=== PAID BY EVERY Moo PROGRAM, WHICH NEVER MENTIONS pack ===

Found while measuring #1910 (a warm Moo class with one `has` costs ~4.4 s).
Main 4c6565e5, quiet box, one fresh `PCL_CACHE_DIR` per case (mode 700).

THE PATH, from an encapsulation of `pcl::p-load-extension` with a backtrace
(scratch/s473x/probes/p1910ext.pl in the s473x worktree):

    EXT-LOAD-START pcl-pack
     0: (P-LOAD-EXTENSION "pcl-pack")
     1: (P-PACK "F" 0)
     2: ("top level form")     <- of ~/.pcl-cache/modules/<hash>.fasl, i.e.
                                  the CACHED FASL of Sub/Quote.pm
    13: (P-USE "Sub::Quote" :IMPORT-ARGS #("quote_sub" "quotify") â¦)
    EXT-LOAD-END pcl-pack 3.978 s

`Sub::Quote`'s top-level code calls `pack("F",0)`.  Moo loads Sub::Quote for
any `has`.  So a Moo class with one attribute pays the whole pack-artifact
recompile, every run, for ever â without the program, or Moo, or Sub::Quote's
author knowing anything about pack.

THE MEASURED PRIZE (scratch/s473x/probes/p1202table.pl; each case its own
fresh cache dir, six warm runs to settle the module fasl ladder, then best of
three; the extension column is a re-run under the encapsulation):

    case                  perl(s)   pcl(s)   extensions loaded
    a strict+warnings       0.004    0.042   none
    b use Moo               0.010    0.067   none
    c Moo + one has         0.014    4.389   pcl-pack 4.015 s
    d mro::get_linear_isa   0.003    0.085   pcl-mro  0.046 s
    e JSON::PP encode       0.013    0.231   none
    f pack("N",1)           0.002    3.598   pcl-pack 3.914 s
    g print "ok"            0.003    0.039   none

Read: caching the extension load would take (c) 4.389 s -> ~0.37 s and (f)
3.598 s -> ~0.10 s, warm.  `pcl-mro` is real but small (46 ms) and
`pcl-warnings` does not load for `use warnings` at all, so the number is
almost entirely `cl/pcl-pack.lisp` â which is also this task's original
measurement (8.3 s at s470bp, on a colder tree), reached from a second
direction.

WHY THE PARK'S REASONING NO LONGER COVERS IT.  The park (USER,
plan-speed-and-ir-s470.md Â§A.0) is "the transpiled oracle and its 3 s
extension load are not touched until the XS question is answered â if pclxs
carries `pack`, that whole cost class goes away without compiler work."  Three
facts moved under it: (i) the cost is NOT confined to pack users â it is the
flagship `use Moo` warm-start number in README and docs/caching.md; (ii)
pclxs is itself parked (USER s485: the three `Pl/t/xs-0N.t` files `plan
skip_all` until pclxs works again), so "the XS decision" is not close; (iii)
the lever is the LOADER, not the oracle â no line of `cl/pcl-pack.lisp` or
`cl/pack-impl.pl` changes, and `pcl-mro`/`pcl-warnings`/`pcl-xs` get it too.

s473x did NOT build it: the park is the USER's own decision and stands until
the USER answers.  The design below is unchanged and is one commit away.


=== PARK LIFTED -- USER RULING (s492, 2026-09-20): "Ah, good that you brought it up. Please put it high on the queue." ===
Scope as Fable proposed it: the LOADER ONLY (`p-load-extension` reuses the #1188 module-fasl machinery; key = the extension file's own CONTENT + *pcl-runtime-identity*; no line of cl/pack-impl.pl or the pack oracle changes; all extensions benefit: pack, mro, warnings, xs).  It takes the FIRST free agent slot, AHEAD of s492b / s492c, as a short batch of its own.  Bar: gate + full sweep (`cl/` change) + a cold / warm / after-editing-the-artifact timing table for `pcl -E 'print pack("N",1)'` and the warm Moo probe `~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/p1910-moo.pl` (before: ~4.0 s of a ~4.5 s warm run), a stale-fasl test (regenerate an artifact -> the next run must recompile, never load the old fasl), `PCL_NO_CORE=1` and an INSTALLED tree (tools/install-pcl) both still work, prune policy = the module cache's (docs/caching.md).  The measured prize table is in the archived s473x STOP.md ("Measured and NOT built") and #1910.


================================================================
=== DONE (s1202, Opus, 2026-09-20) ===

SHIPPED, LOADER ONLY, on main 093732ab.  No line of cl/pack-impl.pl or of any
artifact changed; no emission change, no generation bump.

WHAT IT IS.  `p-load-extension` keeps its contract (idempotent per name, NIL
when the file is absent, %pcl-check-extension-clean after the load) and
delegates the load to %p-load-extension-file, which resolves

    <cache>/ext/<name>-<content stem>-<runtime identity>.fasl
    stem = sxhash(<name> NUL <the extension file's bytes>)

loads it with %p-load-module-fasl when it is there, else builds it with
%p-build-module-fasl and loads that, else falls back to the text `load` --
exactly today's path.  <cache>/ext/ is a fourth directory in the ONE prune;
%p-compile-module-p gains an :extension class beside :main-script; a
successful build deletes the other entries for the same NAME and the same
RUNTIME IDENTITY.  Normative: docs/ir-spec.md section 9.2c; prose in
docs/caching.md section 4 and docs/extensions.md.

THE FIVE DESIGN QUESTIONS, ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT.

(1) Does an artifact contain anything *pcl-fasl-build* does not cover?  NO.
The three transpiled artifacts are exactly the module vocabulary the flag is
written for (p-defpackage / p-declare-sub / p-defcell / p-sub /
p-eval-always (p-note-inc ...) / p-run-compile-phase-blocks) plus plain
defun/defvar in pack's hand-written appendix; no eval-when, no defconstant,
no #., no defmacro anywhere in them.  All four compile with failure-p NIL and
answer identically from the fasl in a FRESH image.

(2) cl/pcl-xs.lisp?  It compiles (0.659 s) and LOADS from a fasl in a fresh
image with its alien routines defined: define-alien-callable and
define-alien-routine expand to ordinary definitions, and load-shared-object
sits inside a function called at run time.  So it is NOT excluded, and the
loader names no extension at all (rule 9a).

(3) Core mode vs PCL_NO_CORE=1: the SAME key.  Measured -- runtime identity
48A74430FEF1 in both, one shared entry, a source-mode run taking a FASL HIT
on a fasl a core-mode run built.  *pcl-runtime-identity* hashes the runtime
SOURCE plus the SBCL and deliberately not the runtime's PATH (only the core's
own name carries that), which is right: the fasl has this runtime's macro
expansions and inlined accessors baked in, and nothing else decides it.  So a
checkout, its worktrees and an install of the same source share one entry.

(4) Racing builds: NO lock.  compile-file writes <name>-tmp<pid>.fasl and
renames, so a reader never sees a partial file and two writers produce the
same bytes.  The waste is bounded at one compile per process, once, on the
first run after a runtime or artifact change -- which is exactly what EVERY
run paid before this task.

(5) Install-time prebuild: FILED as #2086, not taken.  For a single-user
install it is one run's worth, the same as a checkout; for the shared
/opt/pcl shape every user pays 4.7 s once and the installing user's prebuild
would land in the installing user's cache.  The shape that works is a
read-only <root>/ext/ beside pcl.core, consulted before the user cache.

MEASURED (this box, a sibling agent running, load 4.3-10; each tree its own
fresh PCL_CACHE_DIR at 0700; WARM = best of 3 after 6 settling runs; COLDX =
one run with <cache>/ext removed).  BASE = a `git archive` extraction of main.

    case                        BASE warm   AFTER warm   BASE coldx  AFTER coldx
    control `print 1`              0.263        0.264       0.267       0.265
    pack("N",1)                    5.588        0.280       5.528       6.587
    mro::get_linear_isa            0.344        0.275       0.339       0.375
    use warnings; enabled()        0.300        0.269       0.324       0.325
    p1910-moo.pl (the s491 probe)  9.723        4.427       9.888      11.096
    Moo + one `has`                5.774        1.050         --          --

    cl/pcl-pack.lisp   TEXT load 4.262 s   FASL load 0.004 s   compile 4.70 s
    cl/pcl-mro.lisp    TEXT 0.050          FASL 0.002          compile 0.045
    cl/pcl-warnings    TEXT 0.028          FASL 0.001          compile 0.026
    key material: read + sxhash of the largest artifact ~1 ms

    after REGENERATING an artifact (a copy of the tree, a comment appended to
    cl/pcl-pack.lisp): first run 6.091 s, the run after that 0.251 s, and
    exactly ONE entry left for pcl-pack -- the superseded one was dropped.

The control row is the one to read beside the others: a program that loads no
extension is UNCHANGED, because p-load-extension does nothing until something
asks.  The p1910-moo row's remaining 4.4 s is that probe's own work (18 module
fasl hits; the extension load is 0.003 s) -- it is a much larger program than
the "Moo + one has" case the prize table was written from.

A SECOND, SMALLER FIX the guard forced out: %p-load-module-fasl's two
NON-BUILD failure arms (an unreadable fasl; one a sibling pruned between the
check and the LOAD) wrote the .failed BUILD marker, which refuses a rebuild
for an hour.  Right after a compile that just failed, wrong for a file a crash
truncated -- one bad fasl cost an hour of loading from text, for modules and
scripts too.  They now announce under PCL_FASL_DEBUG and rebuild.

BAR: gate Result: PASS 250 files / 8495 tests; full sweep --jobs 4 GATE clean,
0 new / 0 fixed, TOTAL passing 18685 (+0), drops 5 = census, pack.t 5636/89
identical to the blessed baseline; tools/t/ext-fasl.t 25 rows, 10 of which
FAIL on a `git archive main` extraction; tools/t/install-pcl.t 57/57 and an
installed tree verified to use the entry; tools/ir-conform --jobs 2 323 pass /
0 fail / 0 stale; check-parens, tag-license --check, ir-inventory identical.
